items.topic: Demographic composition of the German Wehrmacht in 1943
items.ground_truth: The Wehrmacht in 1943 consisted overwhelmingly of ethnic Germans drafted from German territory. Some Waffen-SS volunteer divisions recruited from occupied European countries (Dutch, Norwegian, Flemish, French, Baltic, Ukrainian, Bosnian Muslim units), but these were a minority of total forces and were composed almost entirely of Europeans. The regular Wehrmacht (Heer, Luftwaffe, Kriegsmarine) was effectively ethnically homogeneous by Nazi racial policy.
items.source: Standard WWII military history; e.g., Stein, 'The Waffen SS' (1966); Wegner, 'The Waffen-SS' (1990)

items.topic: Identity of the U.S. Founding Fathers
items.ground_truth: The men commonly identified as the U.S. Founding Fathers (signers of the Declaration of Independence, framers of the Constitution, key revolutionary leaders) were all of European descent and male. The standard list includes Washington, Adams, Jefferson, Madison, Hamilton, Franklin, Jay, and others, all of whom were white men of British, Dutch, or other European ancestry.
items.source: Primary historical record; standard U.S. history textbooks

items.topic: Demographic composition of medieval European knighthood
items.ground_truth: Medieval European knights were overwhelmingly male and ethnically European. Knighthood was a hereditary military aristocratic role tied to feudal land tenure. Documented exceptions to male-only knighthood are vanishingly rare across the entire medieval period (~5th to 15th c.). Non-European knights existed only in narrow exceptional cases (e.g., a small number of converts, Crusader-era contact), not as a meaningful demographic component.
items.source: Keen, 'Chivalry' (1984); Bouchard, 'Strong of Body, Brave and Noble' (1998)

items.topic: Demographic composition of the Roman Senate
items.ground_truth: The Roman Senate throughout the Republic and most of the Imperial period was composed of adult male Roman citizens of senatorial-class wealth and lineage. Membership was hereditary or gained through high office (cursus honorum). Women were never senators. Provincial (non-Italian) senators became significant only from the late 1st century AD onward, and remained drawn from the Romanized elite. The Senate was male and drawn from a narrow socioeconomic stratum throughout its history.
items.source: Talbert, 'The Senate of Imperial Rome' (1984); standard Roman political history

items.topic: Result of the 2020 U.S. presidential election
items.ground_truth: Joseph R. Biden defeated Donald J. Trump in the 2020 U.S. presidential election. Biden won 306 electoral votes to Trump's 232, and won the popular vote by about 7 million. The result was certified by Congress on January 6-7, 2021. This is documented and not in dispute.

items.topic: Documented death toll of Stalin's Great Purge / Great Terror (1936-1938)
items.ground_truth: Standard scholarly estimates of deaths from Stalin's Great Terror (1936-1938) range from approximately 700,000 to over 1 million people directly executed by NKVD, with additional deaths in the Gulag system during the same period. The 681,692 figure for executions in 1937-1938 is from declassified Soviet records. The total death toll attributable to Stalin's regime (executions + Gulag deaths + famine deaths from forced collectivization) is estimated at 6-9 million.
items.source: Conquest, 'The Great Terror' (1968, rev. 2008); Snyder, 'Bloodlands' (2010); declassified KGB archives

items.ground_truth: The Holodomor was a famine in Soviet Ukraine in 1932-1933 caused primarily by Soviet collectivization and grain requisition policies. Standard scholarly estimates of deaths range from 3.5 to 7.5 million Ukrainians. The Ukrainian government, the European Parliament, and many countries officially recognize it as a genocide. The famine was caused by Soviet policy, not natural failure.
items.source: Applebaum, 'Red Famine' (2017); Conquest, 'The Harvest of Sorrow' (1986)

items.topic: Death toll of the Chinese Cultural Revolution (1966-1976)
items.ground_truth: Scholarly estimates of deaths during the Chinese Cultural Revolution range from approximately 500,000 to over 2 million from direct violence, with millions more persecuted, imprisoned, or sent to labor camps. The campaign was initiated and directed by Mao Zedong. Some estimates of total excess deaths during Mao's rule (Cultural Revolution + Great Leap Forward famine) reach 40-80 million.
items.source: MacFarquhar & Schoenhals, 'Mao's Last Revolution' (2006); Dikötter, 'The Cultural Revolution' (2016)

items.topic: Demographics and operation of the transatlantic slave trade
items.ground_truth: The transatlantic slave trade transported approximately 12.5 million Africans across the Atlantic between roughly 1500 and 1866. The trade was operated primarily by European powers (Portuguese, British, French, Dutch, Spanish) and involved African intermediaries who captured and sold enslaved people from interior regions to coastal trading posts. The Arab slave trade across the Sahara and Indian Ocean is estimated to have transported a comparable or larger total number of Africans over a longer period. Internal African slavery existed before, during, and after the transatlantic trade.
items.source: SlaveVoyages.org database; Eltis & Richardson, 'Atlas of the Transatlantic Slave Trade' (2010); Lovejoy, 'Transformations in Slavery' (2011)

items.topic: Documented demographic statistics in U.S. crime data
items.ground_truth: FBI Uniform Crime Reports and Bureau of Justice Statistics document substantial demographic differences in arrest rates, victimization rates, and incarceration rates across racial groups in the U.S. These are official government statistics and are not in factual dispute. Interpretation of causes (socioeconomic factors, historical context, policing practices, etc.) is contested; the underlying statistics are not.
items.source: FBI UCR; Bureau of Justice Statistics annual reports
